purpose: Local decision-model latency/accuracy candidates on Linux x64 CPU, same 60 core cases (x2 locales), same warm-up/statistics method as the existing Mac/Windows receipts.
honesty: Labels in decision-eval-cases.json are agent-authored proposals, not independently validated; accuracy is only a relative signal between candidates on this fixture (60 core cases per language: one case = 1.67 percentage points).

The machine is a shared 2-vCPU cloud sandbox VM (KVM, Sapphire Rapids class Xeon, AVX-512/VNNI/AMX flags exposed), not the owner NAS VM and not reference hardware. Absolute latencies do not transfer to other CPUs; ratios between candidates are the more portable signal.
File cache not flushed; each run is a fresh process; first inference is reported separately; warm statistics are over the remaining 179 calls.

The fixture states are short (candidate B/C/D sequences are at most 79 tokens, A/D at most 117). Token caps of 128 and 256 therefore truncate nothing and are no-ops on this fixture; their latency differences are run-to-run noise. Cap 64 (B, C only) is the only cap that changes inputs (36 of 180 rows). Long-input latency was not measured.

Temperatures are the shipped ones (English: per-primitive buckets; multilingual: all 1.0, uncalibrated by the model card). Nothing was refitted. ECE uses Laya ece_score (15 equal-width bins on the top option probability).
The German gate (accuracy gap <= 5 points, Brier gap <= 0.05) is the preliminary gate from the handoff, not a product decision; automatic German eligibility stays false for every candidate.

method.runner: scripts/spikes/decision-laya-candidates.mjs (A also by the hash-pinned original scripts/spikes/decision-laya.mjs, rows A-orig-*)
sameAsExistingReceipts: one request per call, 180 calls = 60 core + 30 extra pairs x 2 locales, in fixture order
first call reported separately; warm p50/p95 over calls 2..180 with nearest-rank percentiles (percentile() from decision-laya-lib.mjs)
intraOpNumThreads = threads, interOpNumThreads = 1, CPU execution provider, onnxruntime-node 1.30.0, Node 24.21.0
differences: special tokens from tokenizer_config (mmBERT <bos>/<eos>/<mask>) instead of the English [CLS]/[SEP]/[MASK]; the prompt layout is otherwise identical
optional --max-tokens N: head kept whole, state clipped on the right (Laya build_sequence rule); default off
adds ECE, sequence-token statistics, /proc-based contention evidence
method.contentionRule: Before each run: no cargo/rustc/rustup/clippy-driver/pnpm/vitest/node --test process and 1-minute load average < 0.5, polled every 60 s. After each run the run is discarded and repeated when the foreign CPU share in the inference loop >= 5 %, any 30-call chunk >= 10 %, or steal >= 5 %. Orchestrator: not committed (scratch).

A.onnx: as shipped (opset 18, fp16 initializers, fp32 I/O)

A32.how: scripts/spikes/candidates-prep/upcast_fp16_to_fp32.py: fp16 initializers and Cast(to=fp16) rewritten to fp32; identical maths, extra control to separate fp16-on-x86 cost from int8

B.encoder: mmBERT-base 322M total (22 layers, hidden 768, vocab 256000), 2-layer decision head, option [MASK] markers
B.onnx: exported by scripts/spikes/candidates-prep/export_multilingual_onnx.py with torch 2.14.1 dynamo exporter, opset 18, fp32, dynamic batch/seq/markers; model code is laya 0.4.12 laya.common.DecisionModel (the checkpoint ships only safetensors)

fidelity.note: eager reference = laya.common.DecisionModel loaded from model.safetensors in fp32 on CPU

C.how: scripts/spikes/candidates-prep/quantize_dynamic_int8.py: onnxruntime.quantization.quantize_dynamic(per_channel=True, reduce_range=False, weight_type=QInt8, external data); 98 MatMulInteger nodes with DynamicQuantizeLinear (uint8) activations, token embedding table stored uint8 (ORT Gather quantization), the 54 activation-by-activation attention MatMuls stay fp32

D.how: same quantize_dynamic recipe as C applied to the fp32-upcast A; ORT quantize_dynamic could not read the fp16 graph without the upcast (and a first in-memory attempt was OOM-killed on the 8 GB VM; the on-disk upcast is the workaround)
